head: We could not tell if less sink makes planted causes easier to find: a model with a sink and one without scored the same
sub: Question: does less attention-sink mass make planted features easier for a sparse autoencoder to find? Not settled. A sink is attention that heads with nothing to read park on the first token. Tiny 4-layer models learned text with 64 planted causes; a sparse autoencoder at the middle layer tried to find them (recovery score, 0 to 1). Across {n_fit} models without a gate, the slope of score on sink mass was {b} (95% range {b_lo} to {b_hi}).
seq_lab: One test sequence. Causes {on} are on. After each trigger ▲, 3 tokens depend on them; other tokens do not.
col_att: At token {q}, the middle layer's attention
grp2: Gather the causes in the middle layer
grp4: Gather the causes only in the last layer
foot: 4-layer transformers (about 200,000 parameters) trained 12,000 steps; sparse autoencoder with 256 entries, 3 seeds; 1,000 test sequences · Kran Lab, Nov 8 2026
